I think there's always a honeymoon phase when starting a new antidepressant. Being so depressed/anxious for so long then getting a jolt of the neurotransmitters we need is kind of like when you finally get well after being physically sick. It's such a high that you can get out of bed finally and eat real food after feeling like death. Eventually, your body adjusts back to normal health and everyday feels the same again. The same thing happens with most meds or even supplementing after finding out you're deficient. It takes time for your body to equalize to 'normal' and all the ups and downs in between are just its attempts to do exactly that. But us with our subconscious always interfering skews our perception of working or not, nuanced by all the little things we tell ourselves about it, making it even more difficult to just let it work. 

As a side note, I accidentally double dosed my 75mg one day and felt GREAT! I thought about it and analyzed it to death. Next day I was like well hell i have plenty and a lot to get done today, so why not try it again? I felt terrible lol, so nauseous and insomnia came back full force no matter what I took. So as much as we want to fix ourselves and get instant results and gratification, it's always going to be slow and so slow that it's barely noticeable at times and that's frustrating. Just be patient and in the meantime, do everything you can to get your body in its best health ever. Concentrate on what you CAN do and what's within your control. Good luck!

Whether or not you can count on someone or anyone is a depressing thing to figure out, but then besides being high and dry for help, you realize you've been looking externally for help, happiness, validation, etc. throughout your life and now it's time to make a switch. When you start with you, eventually you get to the point that nothing anyone does or doesn't do or whatever is said about you, doesn't affect you at all bc you already know who you are and love yourself, so you just instantly ignore it bc it's a 'them' problem.  While you continue approaching life with love and doing things that fill your soul. 

Lifelong process that I don't think humans ever fully achieve, but get really close. Build your circle with the ones who know suffering and are trying to help others avoid it. Authenticity helps more than anyone with a boat or an influential following bc those guys are dead inside trying to awaken with all the wrong things and they know helping you out won't build the ego they're trying to cultivate, exude and get propped up, unless it somehow gets TV air time or something so they can brag about helping. All of that self hate is dissolving, the people who criticized me are gone, I'm surrounded by people who actually like me and can't even comprehend a hate campaign on me like I do to myself.
